stem:
A physiologist measures pressures across the glomerular capillaries of a healthy 28-year-old woman: glomerular blood hydrostatic pressure 55 mm Hg, capsular hydrostatic pressure 15 mm Hg, and blood colloid osmotic pressure 30 mm Hg.

Which of the following is her net filtration pressure?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Only the capsular pressure was subtracted; the osmotic force was ignored.
options.explanation: Subtracting only the capsular hydrostatic pressure gives 40 mm Hg, but the blood colloid osmotic pressure also opposes filtration and must be subtracted as well.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Only the colloid osmotic pressure was subtracted; the capsular pressure was ignored.
options.explanation: Subtracting only the osmotic pressure gives 25 mm Hg; both the capsular hydrostatic and the colloid osmotic pressures oppose filtration and must both be subtracted.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; NFP = GBHP − (CHP + BCOP) = 55 − (15 + 30) = 10 mm Hg.
options.explanation: Net filtration pressure equals glomerular blood hydrostatic pressure minus the sum of capsular hydrostatic pressure and blood colloid osmotic pressure: 55 − (15 + 30) = 10 mm Hg, driving fluid into Bowman's space.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The opposing pressures were added to, rather than subtracted from, the hydrostatic pressure.
options.explanation: Adding all three pressures gives 100 mm Hg, but capsular hydrostatic and colloid osmotic pressures oppose the glomerular hydrostatic pressure and are subtracted.

options.label: E
options.misconception: The direction of the net force is being reversed.
options.explanation: The glomerular hydrostatic pressure exceeds the combined opposing pressures, so the 10 mm Hg net pressure drives fluid out of the capillary — filtration, not reabsorption.

context: Learning objective: compute net filtration pressure. NFP = GBHP − (CHP + BCOP), normally about 10 mm Hg favoring filtration.
imageCaption: Nephron segments: filtration, PCT, loop, DCT, collecting duct (ADH aquaporins).
